back_translation: I said within my heart, “Come, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good.” But behold, this too was without substance.
I said of laughter, “It is madness,” and of pleasure, “What does it give?”

I pondered in my heart how to indulge my body with wine — while my heart was still guiding me with wisdom — and how to take hold of folly, until I could see what is good for the sons of men to do under heaven during the few short days of their lives.
I did great works. I built many houses and planted many vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted fruit trees of every kind in them.
I made many pools of water for myself, to water the groves of trees flourishing in the forest.
I bought male slaves and female slaves, and had slaves born in my house. I also had many herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
I accumulated for myself silver and gold, including the precious treasure of kings and provinces. I had male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men — many concubines.
So I became great and increased more than all who were in Jerusalem before me, and my wisdom still remained with me.
Whatever my eyes desired, I never withheld. I did not restrain my heart from any pleasure, for my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.

But when I considered all the works that my hands had done, and the toil I had labored to accomplish, behold, everything was without substance, a chasing after the wind; there was no gain at all under the sun.
Then I turned to consider wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what more can the one who comes after the king do, except what has already been done?
I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, just as light has an advantage over darkness.
The wise man has his eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also realized that the same event happens to them all.
So I said within my heart, “What happens to the fool will happen to me also; why then have I been wiser?” And I said within my heart that this too is without substance.
For the wise man, like the fool, will not be remembered forever; in the days to come everything will already be forgotten. How can the wise man die just like the fool!
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was a misery to me, for everything is without substance, a chasing after the wind.
I hated all my toil at which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the one who comes after me.
And who knows whether that man will be wise or a fool? Yet he will take possession of all the toil at which I labored and used wisdom under the sun. This too is without substance.
So I turned back and let my heart despair over all the toil at which I had toiled under the sun.
For there is a man who toils with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and then must hand over his portion to one who did not toil for it at all. This too is without substance and a great evil.
For what does a man get from all his toil and from the striving of his heart, at which he toils under the sun?
For all his days are full of pain, and his task is sorrow; even at night his heart does not rest. This too is without substance.
For man, there is nothing better than to eat, to drink, and to let his soul enjoy good in his toil. I saw also that this comes from the hand of God.
For who can eat, or who can find enjoyment, apart from me?

For God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the one who pleases Him, but He assigns to the sinner the task of gathering and collecting, in order to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is without substance, a chasing after the wind.
